title: Adaptation of a laboratory protocol to quantity microplastics contamination in estuarine waters
author: Rodrigues, R. Almeida, et al.

steps.title: Prepare microplastic test particles
steps.instruction: Manually cut film plastic bags (LDPE, specific gravity 0.93 g/cm³) and bottle‑cap fragments (PET, specific gravity 1.37 g/cm³) and fishing‑line fibers (PA, specific gravity 1.13 g/cm³); sieve each material through a 5 mm mesh to discard particles larger than 5 mm; for the <5 mm fractions subdivide into two size classes: 3–5 mm and <2 mm; obtain 1 mm high‑density polyethylene (PE‑HD) microspheres commercially (Cospheric Innovations) and use as received; weigh an initial mass of 0.5 mg of each polymer type per sample; prepare six replicates for each polymer type.

substeps.instruction: Manually cut LDPE bags, PET bottle‑cap pieces, and PA fishing‑line fibers.
Sieve each material through a 5 mm mesh to remove particles >5 mm.
Separate the <5 mm material into 3–5 mm and <2 mm size fractions.
Obtain 1 mm PE‑HD microspheres commercially and keep unchanged.
Weigh 0.5 mg of each polymer type for each sample.
Prepare six replicates per polymer type.

steps.title: Collect and pre‑filter water sample
steps.instruction: Collect estuarine water from the Douro estuary and pass the sample through a 5 mm mesh sieve to retain particles ≤5 mm for further processing.

steps.title: Sieving and drying (Phase 1)
steps.instruction: Place the material retained on the 5 mm sieve into a pre‑weighed glass dish and dry it until a constant weight is reached (drying conditions as described in the NOAA protocol).

steps.title: Organic matter elimination (Phase 2)
steps.instruction: Add hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) to the dried sample and perform hot digestion (temperature and concentration as used in the NOAA protocol or as optimized for estuarine water) to oxidize all organic matter; allow the digestion to complete before proceeding.

steps.title: Density separation (Phase 3)
steps.instruction: Add saturated sodium chloride solution to the digested sample, mix thoroughly, and let the mixture settle; collect the floating microplastics, noting that NaCl may be less efficient for estuarine waters and could lead to under‑estimation of MP concentration.
